summary: A status report from SRI's Augmentation Research Center and Network Information Center. Its conversion to a PDP-10 running TENEX was nearly done after some obscure bugs, including a noisy ground traced to bad memory data. Reliability was about one crash every day or two, and work turned to network software.

plainLanguage.summary: SRI reports on preparing its new TENEX system to serve network users. It outlines a gradual service rollout and explains how the Network Information Center handles documents and catalogs.

subtitle: SRI reports on its system conversion, network service plans and NIC operations.

tldr.problem: SRI's Augmentation Research Center and Network Information Center were preparing to provide network access while tuning a newly converted computer system.
tldr.mechanism: The report describes the remaining network software work and a staged service plan, from a small trial to broader access and added features.
tldr.outcome: The planned stages offered increasing NIC services, while the report also covered document distribution and catalog work.

today: RFC 153 is a status report published in May 1971. The unit metadata lists its status as Unknown.

sections.title: System Conversion and Capacity
sections.content:
SRI had nearly completed conversion to a PDP-10 running TENEX. A memory problem traced to a noisy ground had been fixed, and reliability had improved to about one crash every day or two. Staff were measuring and tuning the system and bringing up an NCP and Telnet.

The report says network service would require more processing than local typewriter use. SRI estimated it might support six network users by mid-summer, with an optimistic possibility of closer to twelve, but the actual effect on response time and file transfers was not yet known.
sections.plainLanguage: SRI had fixed a hardware problem and was preparing its network software. It did not yet know how many network users the system could handle reliably.

sections.title: Three Planned Service Stages
sections.content:
Stage 0, planned for June 18, offered experimental access to a limited number of West Coast sites. It included the TENEX Executive, NICTNLS, an initial dialog support system and a first users manual, with at most two network users at once.

Stage 1, planned for August 2, would open access to any network site with the needed software and add online documents. Stage 2, planned for September 6, would add remote message delivery, deferred file preparation and improved queries. These were plans conditional on technical progress and protocol availability.
sections.plainLanguage: SRI planned to start with a small trial, then open access more widely. Later stages were to add document access, message delivery and ways to prepare files before using them.

sections.title: NIC Documents and Catalogs
sections.content:
The report describes the NIC's offline work distributing RFCs and other materials to liaison people and station agents. It asks contributors to send a good copy for duplication and emphasizes assigning each document a unique number, including when it updates an earlier document.

The NIC was working to bring its catalog up to date and expected to issue it monthly. The report points readers to RFCs 115 and 118 for site documentation recommendations.
sections.plainLanguage: The NIC distributed documents, maintained a catalog and asked each new document to have its own number. It also invited sites to suggest ways to improve its service.
